images.title: Why the largest digit multiplies
images.purpose: Shows that for digits p < q < r, qp × r and rp × q share the part 10qr, and the ones part pr beats pq.
images.composition: Two lines of working, one above the other, with matching parts lined up, and one number check beneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Top centre, small: p < q < r in dark text. Line 1: qp × r = 10qr + pr, with qp × r in dark text, 10qr in grey (#6B7280), and pr in green (#009E73). Line 2 directly below: rp × q = 10qr + pq, with rp × q in dark text, 10qr in grey directly under the first 10qr, and pq in vermilion (#D55E00) directly under pr. Below both lines, centred, the check 64 × 8 = 512 in reddish purple (#CC79A7). Exactly 2 lines of working and 1 check; no tiles, no arrows.

images.takeaway: Both have 10qr; pr is bigger than pq, so qp × r wins.
images.description: Shows that for digits p < q < r, qp × r and rp × q share the part 10qr, and the ones part pr beats pq.

image_decisions.why: Lining up the two expansions in one picture shows the equal part and the deciding part at a glance.
